question.text: An insurance company uses exchange-traded interest rate futures to hedge the reinvestment risk on expected premium income (a listed forecasted transaction). The profit from these futures should be accounted for as:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 296 of the NISM Series IV workbook, insurance entities follow the accounting treatment prescribed by IRDAI, if any. Pages 285-286 confirm IRDAI permits insurance companies to use IRF only for long hedges of listed forecasted transactions and for hedging interest-rate risk, which fits the reinvestment-of-expected-premium-income scenario. The Trap: While general accounting may classify exchange-traded IRD income as business income, insurance companies are regulated entities. If IRDAI has prescribed a specific treatment, that overrides the general Guidance Note. Where no regulator-prescribed treatment exists, the ICAI Guidance Note applies. Note: Source-backed rule from page 296 of Series IV: insurance entities follow IRDAI-prescribed treatment for derivative contracts. The permitted IRF hedge use cases per pages 285-286 include long hedges of listed forecasted transactions such as expected premium income or reinvestment of maturity proceeds.
